conventions: Regnal age formula. In `בֶּן` + numeral + `שָׁנָה` + name, the construct `בֵּן` is the clause's predicate: it takes the construction-supplied copula together with the English 'old' (rule 20), discontinuous around the numeral phrase under rule 25, while `שָׁנָה` takes 'years', the numerals take their own words and the king's name takes only its own. 2CH.33.1 `בֶּן־שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה מְנַשֶּׁה` and 2CH.33.21 `בֶּן־עֶשְׂרִים וּשְׁתַּיִם שָׁנָה אָמוֹן` are aligned identically. Do not attach 'was' to the subject name, and do not read 'old' as the counted noun's.

Source-citation formula. The chapter writes it both ways and they divide differently. Where the Hebrew writes no verb (2CH.33.18 `הִנָּם עַל־דִּבְרֵי מַלְכֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל`), the prepositional phrase is the predicate and takes the construction-supplied copula on `עַל` under rule 49, headed on 'among', while the ASV's supplied lexical 'written' is its own `added` unit under rule 20. Where the Hebrew writes `כְּתוּבִים` (2CH.33.19), that participle takes 'are written' and `עַל` keeps only the 'in' written for its own relation. Read which shape the verse has before placing the copula.

An adversative or restrictive particle standing in the clause is itself what a written 'but' says and takes it, so the word is not `added` under rule 14's closing sentences: `רַק` takes the whole 'but only' at 2CH.33.17 and `כִּי` takes 'but' at 2CH.33.23, as `אֲבָל` takes 'Nevertheless' at 2CH.33.17. This reaches a particle whose own sense is adversative, not a coordinator supplied for a clause no such morpheme stands in - the 'how' of 2CH.33.19 is `added`, because the only conjunction in that clause is a waw already holding the 'and' written for it.

Line drawn on words the ASV writes inside a verb's rendering. Phrasal particles were kept whole with the verb throughout - `בָּנָה` -> 'built up' (33.16), `קוּם` hiphil -> 'reared up' (33.3), `סוּר` -> 'took away' (33.15), `עָמַד` hiphil -> 'set up' (33.19), `סָבַב` -> 'compassed about' (33.14), `שׁוּב` hiphil -> 'brought again' (33.13) - each discontinuous under rule 25 where the object intervenes and each headed on the lexical verb. Supplied objects and adjuncts were not: 'them' at 33.15 and 'with it' at 33.14 are `added` under rules 44 and 30, no object morpheme standing in either clause. The competing reading on 'built up', that rule 44's subtraction makes the particle a surplus because bare 'built' already writes banah, is recorded in that verse's note.
report: Read all 25 verses end to end against the 52-lemma candidate table. No genuine cross-verse split found: every multi-treatment bucket is the ASV rendering one morpheme differently in different contexts, with something in the source licensing the difference.

Article counting in construct chains is the chapter's largest recurring family (13 phrases) and is uniform under rule 29. Arthrous on both sides (toavot ha-goyim 33.2, pesel ha-semel 33.7, sarey ha-tsava 33.11, divrey ha-hozim 33.18, am ha-arets 33.25 twice) gives the written 'the' to the article and a supplied one to the construct; anarthrous rectum (tseva ha-shamayim 33.3 and 33.5, beyt ha-elohim 33.7) fronts the article's 'the'. The five Td-unrepresented tokens (33.6, 33.7, 33.13, 33.14, 33.25) are determiner counts under rules 41 and 47, not a second treatment.

Checked individually and found licensed: ra/ha-ra ('that which was evil' 33.2 and 33.22 against bare 'evil' 33.6 and 33.9, the latter with no article at all); bamah headed on 'high' in 33.3, 33.17, 33.19; pesel/pesil headed on 'graven' in 33.7, 33.19, 33.22; mi-pney, mi-li-pney and li-pney fused in 33.2, 33.9, 33.12, 33.19, 33.23; kana with its reflexive in 33.12, 33.19, 33.23; hinnam plus suffix in 33.18 and 33.19; the ben-shanah age idiom in 33.1 and 33.21; tachtav as 'in ... stead' in 33.20 and 33.25.

The 75 waw tokens are all read off the ASV as rule 14 directs. The one unrepresented waw (33.3 s003) is the second verb of wayyashov wayyiven, where the ASV writes a single clause and 'again' goes to shuv; the waw-as-relative 'who' (33.11) is rule 17's settled reading; both postposed 'also' words (33.6, 33.19) go to a present waw as rule 51 requires.

raq is not split: 'only' in 33.8 because im holds the written 'if', 'but only' in 33.17 because no conjunction morpheme stands in that clause and raq is itself an adversative-restrictive particle, exactly as rule 14 lets ki carry the 'but' it takes in 33.23.

The six added units were audited against the places where a supplied word was instead folded in. 'given' (33.8), 'with it' (33.14), 'them' (33.15), 'written' (33.18), 'how' and 'God' (33.19) answer to no morpheme; the second 'did' of 33.9 is the one written infinitive realized twice under rules 25 and 34, and the second 'with' of 33.6 is the distributed repetition of the preposition the English verb needs for its object. No supplied word is marked added in one verse and folded in elsewhere.

BSB disagreements: none is a genuine error. All thirteen fall in the documented convention families - prepositions the ASV's recasting leaves with no English word (33.3, 33.6, 33.8, 33.12, 33.14, 33.16, rules 40 and 52), article morphemes the phrase's single determiner does not reach (rules 29, 41, 47), the object marker at 33.25 (rule 16's majority ruling), and the surplus waw at 33.3. BSB attaches each to its host phrase, which is its convention rather than a correction.

One edge a later reader may want to revisit, left as the verse pass accepted it: 33.16 'built up'. Rule 44's subtraction leans toward marking 'up' added, since bare 'built' already writes banah's lexeme, and the verse note names that competing reading. It stands because the chapter keeps every such particle with its verb (reared up 33.3, took away 33.15, set up 33.19, compassed about 33.14, brought again 33.13); changing this one alone would create the split I was asked to find. Convention 4 records the line.
